question.problem: The solution to the inequality $-2x+10\ge 4$ is $x${{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $10$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+10 & \ge 4 \\ -2x+10-10 & \ge 4-10 \\ -2x+0 & \ge -6 \\ -2x & \ge -6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x\,\, & \ge \,\,-6 \\ \frac{-2x}{-2}\, & \le \,\,\frac{-6}{-2} \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}x}{\cancel{-2}}\, & \le \,\,3 \\ x\,\, & \le \,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x\le 3.$
